scope: Five supplemental challenges to the preserved 27 v21 and five v23 claim records; not independent studies.

claims.claim: The missing BUB1B CRISPR evidence cannot be obtained from public data.
claims.support: The frozen v23 panel contains no BUB1B CRISPR record.
claims.challenge: The newer public release contains 31 BUB1B CRISPR profiles across 19 contexts, all from one guide ID.
claims.disposition: Narrow the old absence statement to its dataset; public orthogonal coverage now exists.
claims.falsifier: Exact metadata/ID or source-well checks reveal the supposed BUB1B records are misassigned or duplicate older BUB1B CRISPR observations.
claims.stop: Do not treat profile count as guide count, independent experiment count or functional confirmation.
claims.reopen: Independently targeted and restored endogenous function in the intended residual-function model.
claims.next_action: Use the new profiles to qualify candidates for orthogonal follow-up, preserving source and guide identity.

claims.claim: The HT29 expression lead is only an RNAi artifact.
claims.support: RNAi seed/batch confounding, finite-reference sensitivity and the earlier failed full filters remain.
claims.challenge: HT29 ranks fourth in both PRIME RNAi/CRISPR retrieval directions; removing BUB1B's measured transcript preserves both ranks. Its repeated CRISPR guide is retrieved first across two batches.
claims.disposition: Strengthen HT29 as an assay-qualification lead while retaining one-guide and tumor-context limits.
claims.falsifier: Independent perturbation/restoration fails to reproduce the endogenous functional deficit, or the expression effect follows editing/general stress rather than BUB1B function.
claims.stop: One guide, one failed-QC batch and a tumor line cannot establish independent-guide or non-cancer-model qualification.
claims.reopen: Reproducible target-specific functional deficit and restoration, with independent controls.
claims.next_action: Prioritize HT29 for the narrow attribution test; develop the non-cancer model separately.

claims.claim: A favorable low-dose everolimus connection supplies the missing rescue evidence.
claims.support: Three reference-matching 0.1-uM profiles pass drug QC and negatively correlate with BUB1B; MCF7 has a relatively specific negative connection and retrieves MTOR first.
claims.challenge: All three BUB1B queries have zero passing profiles. MCF7 RNAi and CRISPR disagree. No direct drug-plus-deficit function is measured; HT29's available exact-ID drug profile fails QC.
claims.disposition: Keep favorable mechanism evidence separate from model qualification and therapeutic rescue.
claims.falsifier: The favorable connection fails independent target engagement or joint functional assays, or useful function worsens despite expression reversal.
claims.stop: Do not combine HT29 model evidence with MCF7 drug evidence into a fictional joint result. Failed safety overrides any expression benefit.
claims.reopen: Qualified deficit and drug response in the same relevant model with prespecified function, fate, recovery and injury endpoints.
claims.next_action: Retain MCF7 as a mechanism comparator only; test the joint contrast after model qualification.

claims.claim: New identifiers or better quality scores establish independent low-dose replication.
claims.support: The newer release has more reference-matching profiles and three passing 0.1-uM profiles in matched contexts.
claims.challenge: A375 and NPC regroup earlier singleton wells under new signature IDs. Exact-ID checks alone miss this reuse; other compound identifiers remain stereochemically unresolved.
claims.disposition: Retain improved aggregation and source coverage without overwriting old results or inflating independence.
claims.falsifier: Well-level provenance or chemistry verification contradicts the assumed grouping or identity.
claims.stop: No cross-ID pooling, clinical exposure inference or independence claim from relabelled/reprocessed observations.
claims.reopen: Independent experimental provenance, verified chemistry and relevant exposure measurements.
claims.next_action: Bind signature IDs, source-well sets, preparation versions and chemistry to each future assay result.

claims.claim: A large GPU campaign materially establishes biological confidence.
claims.support: Eight H100 workers complete 2,474,445,074 comparisons with original-coordinate numerical checks.
claims.challenge: Comparisons share profiles; repeated representations are not replication. Timed matrix work is brief and one-second monitoring peaks at 8 percent. No protein function, clinical exposure or joint rescue is established.
claims.disposition: Use compute to expose specificity, context and provenance limits; do not promote biological claims from scale or software success.
claims.falsifier: Numerical, provenance or metadata audits fail, or the biological model fails despite consistent scores.
claims.stop: Any failed integrity check invalidates its derived claim. Additional correlated scores cannot bypass unknown biology.
claims.reopen: Verified computation plus independently qualified biological evidence addressing the specific claim.
claims.next_action: Keep full result tables and uncertainty; spend the next discriminating effort on target/function qualification.
